versions.changelog: 1.5.11: review follow-ups to 1.5.10. Config version 3 reconciles the manifest with the WSL-discovery setting on load whatever version wrote the home (retried while the manifest cannot be inspected), and sets a scheduled consent aside only when the scanned scope actually changed; legacy archive directories are accepted only with complete index schemas backed by real tables; SQLite index paths are percent-encoded.

1.5.10: review follow-ups to 1.5.9. An unmarked directory is accepted as a legacy archive only when its index has the archive schema and holds nothing but host directories; credential-row purges validate host names and containment and keep unsafe rows as unremovable; withdrawing the legacy WSL default also removes WSL hosts from the manifest and sets any scheduled-run consent aside until re-confirmed; the archive path is validated before onboarding writes anything.

1.5.9: review follow-ups to 1.5.8. Credential-like archive rows are purged only once their file is confirmed removed (either storage mode) and archive status reports the post-purge state; a pre-1.5.8 config's implicit WSL-discovery default is withdrawn unless the operator chose it (config version 2); the raw-log archive requires a dedicated directory so removal instructions never touch unrelated data.

1.5.8: the ClawHub / SkillSpector audit of 1.5.7 split into issues #11-#20 and resolved: study_url validated to HTTPS and rendered via DOM APIs; prompt text capture is an explicit opt-in (default off); the generic JSON sniffer refuses broad roots and skips credential-like files; narrowed trigger phrases plus a Before You Start disclosure; authorization and minimisation boundaries in the discovery guide and templates; a sensitivity notice in every study package with paths redacted from ledger.json unless requested; owner-only permissions for every generated run file; no catch-all attribution rules (unmatched calls reported as unattributed); subprocess and data text cleaned before printing; one credential-file predicate across every archive path including legacy rows; WSL discovery default off; SSH transfers disclosed explicitly.

1.5.7: audits of 1.5.4 and 1.5.5 plus four Codex review rounds. Credential files are read only after an explicit opt-in and a warning naming the files; accounts are pseudonymous unless identifiable output is requested; placeholders bill as unknown. Scheduled persistence needs a typed confirmation or an operator-written consent record tied to a hash of the complete manifest, flags and schedule; scheduled runs refuse when anything changed or one-shot options are passed; optional expiry removes the entry. ledger.py publish-check scans directories, zips, DOCX and PDF (unscannable documents fail) for e-mails, account ids, organisation names, host names, credential paths and secret keys. SHA256SUMS covers optional package files; report narrative reflects how accounts were drafted.

Metadata correction: restores the display name to AI Usage Ledger Skill. No functional change from 1.5.4, which carried the T09 manifest-ownership fix, the local-interpreter validation, the documentation corrections and the neutral-path example renders.

Security: the pipeline manifest is executable configuration (it selects interpreters, SSH targets and filesystem roots), so a group- or world-writable manifest is now refused before it is read rather than only warned about, matching the ledger config. local/share hosts additionally validate a manifest-supplied interpreter, closing the gap that ssh and wsl hosts already closed. Addresses ClawHub audit finding T09 on 1.5.3; verified end to end on POSIX with a regression test. Docs: the brand.logo row no longer contradicts the local-file rule, and the local-only claim now notes that an opted-in rendered page can reference a remote logo or Google Fonts stylesheet. Examples: the committed demonstration renders were regenerated from a neutral path so they no longer carry the publisher's local directory.

1.5.3: WSL scans retry wsl.exe three times before falling back to the \wsl$ share, previous scan outputs are cleared before each attempt so a stale inventory cannot pass as success, and every inventory root records its own files, bytes and errors so Codex coverage can be checked against a native rollout count (pitfall 17).

1.5.2: second audit round. Default branding is neutral (no publisher identity); the CompleteTech brand is a named preset applied only on explicit request; run refuses to start unconfigured. Raw-log archive: host names, source paths and destinations validated with realpath containment on archive and restore; SSH archive validates the target and uses fixed remote commands (xargs -0 stat, tar --null -T -) fed NUL-delimited lists, no remote scripts built from paths. Ledger home, store, archive, logs, config and anonymisation map created owner-only (0700/0600); shared or foreign-owned configs refused; accounts.json kept out of study packages unless requested; branded example artefacts excluded from the bundle. tests/test_security.py extended; POSIX permission checks verified on Linux.

1.5.1: security fixes for the ClawHub audit of 1.5.0. Python merge sort replaces the shell sort; SSH/WSL manifest fields validated against strict grammars and quoted, local commands are argument lists only; scheduler wrapper carries fixed flags only, quoted, mode 0700, shown before registration; branding HTML-escaped and validated, logos inlined from local files; generated pages carry a Content-Security-Policy and load nothing from the network (Google Fonts links removed); warnings on group/world-writable config; tests/test_security.py added to the quality gate.

1.5.0: append-only ledger store (SQLite/JSON/CSV) with one-time onboarding and OS-aware harness detection across Windows, macOS, Linux, WSL and SSH hosts; 14 parsers plus a generic sniffer; list-price valuation, cache savings, per-account subscription comparison; branded light/dark dashboard and research-grade study package; 15 ledger document templates (Markdown/HTML/PDF/DOCX); anonymised publication copy; optional raw-log archive; scheduled refresh (Task Scheduler/cron); query layer for detailed questions.
